helpers.purpose: Audit tracked interactions against the call graph the code makes, for the callers in scope. Read-only. Expected edges: calls AND functions used as values (map(fn, xs), partial, dispatch dicts built in the body), credited through untracked same-file helpers, resolved through imports, aliases and re-exports. Categories: missing_interactions (code makes it, DB lacks it), stale_interactions (provably gone: every use of the target's name in the caller resolves to something else — another function, a local or loop variable, a method on a value — or there is none), repoint_interactions (a stale edge that is the same dependency moved: call moved to another function in the same file, or target moved under the same name — one change, not delete+add), unconfirmed_interactions (may be real but unprovable, each with a reason: name resolves ambiguously, called through a record field or factory the target is stored under elsewhere, a callback parameter of the target's name, the name in a string, a non-Python target: mark indirect or delete), indirect_interactions (is_indirect edges) and non_call_interactions (chain/compose/pipe/borrow types): informational, never flagged. Confirmed without being expected (never reported, never asked to be added): self-recursion, functions held in a module-level table the caller reads (dispatch), a non-Python function called as name( in the caller's string literals (SQL). Python callers only (full fidelity); other files listed in unchecked_files. Scope selectors combine as a union; with none, the whole project (tracked files plus untracked source files) is audited. Writes the full report to <project folder>/audit/ and returns counts + samples + report_path.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error when a selector cannot be resolved (unknown git ref, task not found, invalid task_type). Unparseable files are listed in unchecked_files, never abort the audit.
return_statements: [when:report_path] The FULL findings are in report_path (JSON: findings.<category> lists every row with IDs). The result shows counts and up to 5 samples per category — read the file for the rest instead of re-running the audit; delete it when done (or apply_audit_fixes(cleanup=true)).
[when:clean=true] No blocking or warning findings in this scope.
[when:scope.schema_1_15=false] This database predates schema 1.15 (no is_indirect / source_hash): run migrate_databases first; indirect marks and description hashes are unavailable until then.

[when:counts.unchecked_files] unchecked_files lists in-scope files no full-fidelity check covered (names_only / none extraction, or untracked). Verify those by reading them; never treat their absence of findings as clean.

[when:counts.repoint_interactions] repoint_interactions: each is ONE existing edge to move (change='source' or 'target', from_function_id -> to_function_id) — a split or moved call. Apply with apply_audit_fixes(report=<report_path>, apply=['repoint_interactions', ...]).

[when:blocking] Blocking categories are fixed mechanically: apply_audit_fixes(reason=..., report=<report_path>, apply=['repoint_interactions','missing_interactions','stale_interactions']). Dry-run first with dry_run=true when the counts are large. Stale edges are provably not made by the code (dispatch tables, record fields, callbacks, recursion and SQL strings are recognized); a purely conceptual link you want to keep (chain data flow) is KEPT by marking it: apply_audit_fixes(mark_indirect_ids=[...]) first — report deletes skip indirect edges — or held back with exclude={'stale_interactions': [ids]}.

[when:counts.unconfirmed_interactions] unconfirmed_interactions need judgement, never auto-apply: each carries a reason saying why the edge may still be real (ambiguous name, record field, callback, string lookup, non-Python target). Deliberate -> mark_indirect_ids; wrong target -> delete_interaction_ids (and add the right edge).
[when:counts.unresolved_calls] unresolved_calls: call names matching several tracked functions, dropped rather than guessed. Add the real edges explicitly if they matter.

used_by_directives.description: Verify the recorded graph: no missing or stale edges remain after add_interactions

helpers.name: apply_audit_fixes

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why these changes are made; recorded in the restore-manifest note.

parameters.name: report
parameters.description: report_path returned by an audit tool (project-relative path, absolute path, or bare file name in the audit folder).

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: Finding categories of the report to apply. missing_interactions=add, stale_interactions=delete (indirect edges kept), repoint_interactions=move source/target, stale_functions/stale_types=delete (cascades recorded; a stale function with moved_to hands its edges and type links to the successor first), param_mismatch=refresh parameters from source keeping descriptions, malformed_json=re-encode once, missing_type_links=link, unbaselined_descriptions=record current code hash (only after reviewing the prose).

parameters.name: add_interactions
parameters.description: Edges to add (interaction_type defaults to 'call').

parameters.name: repoint_interactions
parameters.description: Edges to move to a new source and/or target.

parameters.name: delete_interaction_ids
parameters.description: Interactions to delete.

parameters.name: mark_indirect_ids
parameters.description: Interactions to mark is_indirect: deliberate edges the code makes indirectly. Audits never flag them; report deletes skip them.

parameters.name: unmark_indirect_ids
parameters.description: Interactions to clear is_indirect on.

parameters.name: delete_function_ids
parameters.description: Functions to delete; their interactions and type links cascade and are recorded in the manifest.

parameters.name: delete_type_ids
parameters.description: Types to delete; their type links cascade and are recorded in the manifest.

parameters.name: refresh_signature_function_ids
parameters.description: Functions whose parameters are re-read from the source (names, order, types, required/default), keeping each surviving parameter's description.

parameters.name: baseline_hash_function_ids
parameters.description: Functions whose current code hash is recorded as matching their description. Only after reviewing purpose/parameters/returns.

parameters.name: add_type_links
parameters.description: types_functions links to add.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Findings of applied categories to hold back (reviewed false positives), as {category: [ids]}: interaction_id for stale/repoint_interactions, function_id for stale_functions/param_mismatch/unbaselined_descriptions, type_id for stale_types, the row id for malformed_json; [source_function_id, target_function_id] pairs for missing_interactions and [type_id, function_id] pairs for missing_type_links. Every category named must also be in apply.

parameters.name: exempt
parameters.description: Reviewed findings that are NOT drift (schema 1.16): [{category, function_id | type_id, reason?}], reason defaulting to the call's. Audits list them under 'exempted' (info) instead of the category, so they stop blocking. A function exemption records the code hash and lapses when the code changes (the finding returns with exemption_lapsed). Edges use mark_indirect_ids instead.

parameters.name: unexempt_ids
parameters.description: audit_exemptions ids (exemption_id in an audit's 'exempted' list) to remove; the finding is reported again. Removed rows go into the manifest.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Do everything, then roll back: the result is exactly what a real run does.

parameters.name: cleanup
parameters.description: Delete the report file after a successful real run.

helpers.purpose: Apply audit findings in ONE call and ONE transaction, with a restore manifest written in the same transaction. Name report categories (report + apply) so thousands of IDs never pass through the conversation, hold back reviewed false positives for this call with exclude={category: [ids]} or for good with exempt=[...], and/or pass explicit changes. Every report finding is re-checked against its row first: an edge whose endpoints changed since the audit, or an entity already gone or renamed, is skipped with a reason. One entry_deletion note lists every deleted row (cascaded edges and type links included) and the old values of every changed row, so any change can be undone. Judgement categories (unconfirmed_interactions, stale_descriptions, dangling_mentions, missing_functions, untracked_files) are refused: they need prose, a mark, or reconcile_paths.
helpers.error_handling: Refuses without a reason, with apply but no report, with non-appliable categories, or with nothing to apply. Any SQL error rolls back everything (nothing partial is ever written).
return_statements: [when:skipped_count] skipped lists rows not changed and why (up to 20; skipped_count is the total) — usually the database moved on since the audit. Re-run the audit for a fresh report if many were skipped.

[when:excluded_count] excluded_count findings were held back by exclude. They stay in the next audit's report; if they are false positives the audit should not raise, say so in a note on the function or edge.
[when:dry_run=true] DRY RUN: nothing was written. Call again with dry_run=false to apply.
[when:applied] Re-run the same audit to confirm the categories you applied are now empty. manifest_note_id is the restore record (get_notes_comprehensive(note_id=...)).
[when:applied.repoint_to_successor] repoint_to_successor moved functions' edges and type links to the function they moved to (moved_to in the report) before deleting them.

helpers.purpose: Audit tracked files, functions and types against the source. Read-only. Python files (full fidelity): missing_functions (public, untracked), stale_functions (tracked, gone from the source; a module-level `f = partial(...)`, lambda or alias binding of the name counts as defined), incomplete_functions (purpose/parameters/returns empty), malformed_json (not one JSON encoding of a list/object; double-encoded is fixable), reserved_functions (never finalized), param_mismatch (recorded parameters vs the signature: names, order, required vs default), missing_types, stale_types (name defined nowhere in the file), incomplete_types, missing_type_links (a tracked type named in a signature with no types_functions link, role suggested), private_tracked and files_without_functions (informational). Every file: missing_files (tracked, gone from disk), untracked_files. Regex languages only report names_only_missing (warning) and never claim anything stale. Untracked _private functions are never reported. Scope selectors combine as a union; with none, the whole project (tracked files plus untracked source files) is audited. Writes the full report to <project folder>/audit/ and returns counts + samples + report_path.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error when a selector cannot be resolved (unknown git ref, task not found, invalid task_type). Unparseable files are listed in unchecked_files, never abort the audit.
return_statements: [when:report_path] The FULL findings are in report_path (JSON: findings.<category> lists every row with IDs). The result shows counts and up to 5 samples per category — read the file for the rest instead of re-running the audit; delete it when done (or apply_audit_fixes(cleanup=true)).
[when:clean=true] No blocking or warning findings in this scope.
[when:scope.schema_1_15=false] This database predates schema 1.15 (no is_indirect / source_hash): run migrate_databases first; indirect marks and description hashes are unavailable until then.

[when:counts.unchecked_files] unchecked_files lists in-scope files no full-fidelity check covered (names_only / none extraction, or untracked). Verify those by reading them; never treat their absence of findings as clean.

[when:counts.untracked_files] untracked_files / missing_functions / missing_types: catalog them in one call with reconcile_paths(paths=<the report's reconcile_paths list>) — it adds signatures and docstring purposes and never overwrites prose — then give new files flows and modules (add_file_flows, add_files_to_module).

[when:counts.stale_functions] stale_functions / stale_types: the code is gone. An entry with moved_to was moved: its old file imports it from moved_to.path, and applying stale_functions hands its edges and type links to moved_to.function_id before deleting it. If it was removed on purpose, apply_audit_fixes(report=<report_path>, apply=['stale_functions','stale_types']) deletes them with every cascaded edge and type link recorded in the restore manifest. If it was renamed, update_function(name=...) keeps the row's prose instead. If the function still exists in a form the audit cannot see (defined inside an if at module level, generated), exempt it: apply_audit_fixes(reason=..., exempt=[{category: 'stale_functions', function_id: N}]).

[when:counts.param_mismatch] param_mismatch: apply_audit_fixes(report=<report_path>, apply=['param_mismatch']) re-reads parameters from the source and keeps each surviving parameter's description; then review the function's purpose in case the behaviour changed with the signature.

[when:counts.malformed_json] malformed_json entries with fixable=true are double-encoded: apply_audit_fixes(apply=['malformed_json']). fixable=false ones need rewriting with update_function / update_type.

[when:counts.incomplete_functions] incomplete_functions / incomplete_types need prose: fill the listed fields with update_function / update_functions_for_file / update_type (a function returning nothing gets returns {"type": "None"}).
[when:counts.missing_type_links] missing_type_links carry a suggested role; check it, then apply_audit_fixes(apply=['missing_type_links']) or add_types_functions with corrected roles.
[when:counts.reserved_functions] reserved_functions were reserved but never finalized: finalize_function(s) if the code exists, else delete them.

[when:counts.exempted] exempted lists findings a person reviewed as not drift (audit_exemptions), with the reason and exemption_id; they never block. A finding carrying exemption_lapsed had an exemption whose function changed since: review it again, then re-exempt (unexempt_ids + exempt) or fix it.
[when:scope.schema_1_16=false] This database predates schema 1.16: run migrate_databases to enable audit exemptions (apply_audit_fixes exempt=[...]).

used_by_directives.description: Verify cataloged functions: empty fields, malformed JSON, parameter drift

helpers.purpose: Audit function and type descriptions for drift from the code. Read-only. stale_descriptions: the function's code changed after its purpose/parameters/returns were written (functions.source_hash, recorded on every prose write, differs from the current code hash; formatting, comments and docstrings never change the hash). dangling_mentions: a description names a callable that exists nowhere — 'name()' or 'snake_name(...)' not defined, imported or called anywhere in the tracked Python files, not tracked, not a builtin or Python keyword, and not vocabulary the code writes in its string literals (a whole-string identifier or 'name(' in a string: DSL built-ins such as jsonencode, parse_json); attribute calls, ALLCAPS and 'file(s)' plurals are ignored. Described functions with no hash yet are triaged against the code: unbaselined_descriptions (info) pass and can be baselined in one call; unbaselined_needs_review (info) carry triage reasons (recorded parameter names or return type differing from the code, a purpose under three words, snake_case/backticked names in the prose the code never uses), the recorded prose and a code excerpt. stale_descriptions carry the same triage and excerpt. Warnings only — never blocks a task. Scope selectors combine as a union; with none, the whole project (tracked files plus untracked source files) is audited. Writes the full report to <project folder>/audit/ and returns counts + samples + report_path.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error when a selector cannot be resolved (unknown git ref, task not found, invalid task_type). On a database before schema 1.15 there are no hashes: only dangling_mentions are checked.
return_statements: [when:report_path] The FULL findings are in report_path (JSON: findings.<category> lists every row with IDs). The result shows counts and up to 5 samples per category — read the file for the rest instead of re-running the audit; delete it when done (or apply_audit_fixes(cleanup=true)).
[when:clean=true] No blocking or warning findings in this scope.
[when:scope.schema_1_15=false] This database predates schema 1.15 (no is_indirect / source_hash): run migrate_databases first; indirect marks and description hashes are unavailable until then.

[when:counts.unchecked_files] unchecked_files lists in-scope files no full-fidelity check covered (names_only / none extraction, or untracked). Verify those by reading them; never treat their absence of findings as clean.

[when:counts.stale_descriptions] stale_descriptions: read each function's code and its purpose/parameters/returns. Wrong -> rewrite with update_function (that records the new hash). Still right -> apply_audit_fixes(baseline_hash_function_ids=[...]) records the current code as described.

[when:counts.dangling_mentions] dangling_mentions: the description names a callable that no longer exists (renamed or removed). Rewrite that sentence with update_function / update_type. A mention that is real vocabulary the audit cannot see (another language's built-in never written in a string) -> apply_audit_fixes(reason, exempt=[{category: 'dangling_mentions', function_id | type_id}]).

[when:counts.unbaselined_descriptions] unbaselined_descriptions passed triage against the code: apply_audit_fixes(report=<report_path>, apply=['unbaselined_descriptions']) records their code hashes in one call (exclude={'unbaselined_descriptions': [ids]} holds back any you want to read first).

[when:counts.unbaselined_needs_review] unbaselined_needs_review: each entry has triage reasons, the recorded prose and a code excerpt — review them in batches from the report. Wrong prose -> update_function / update_functions_for_file (writing prose records the hash). Prose that is fine -> apply_audit_fixes(baseline_hash_function_ids=[...]). A triage flag that is a false positive (the name is a field of a record the function returns) needs no exemption: baselining clears it.

[when:counts.exempted] exempted lists findings a person reviewed as not drift (audit_exemptions), with the reason and exemption_id; they never block. A finding carrying exemption_lapsed had an exemption whose function changed since: review it again, then re-exempt (unexempt_ids + exempt) or fix it.
[when:scope.schema_1_16=false] This database predates schema 1.16: run migrate_databases to enable audit exemptions (apply_audit_fixes exempt=[...]).

helpers.purpose: Run EVERY tracking audit over one scope with one code index and one report: files, functions, types, parameters, JSON encoding, type links (audit_functions), interactions with repoints (audit_interactions), stale prose and dangling mentions (audit_descriptions), plus modularity gaps (structure_gaps). Read-only. The same audit gates task/subtask/sidequest completion (over the item's linked files), runs in aimfp_end over uncommitted work, runs per changed file in the watchdog, and runs in CI as `aimfp audit`. Scope selectors combine as a union; with none, the whole project (tracked files plus untracked source files) is audited. Writes the full report to <project folder>/audit/ and returns counts + samples + block/warn verdict + report_path.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error for an unknown include name or a selector that cannot be resolved (unknown git ref, task not found, invalid task_type).

The result shows counts and up to 5 samples per category — read the file for the rest instead of re-running the audit; delete it when done (or apply_audit_fixes(cleanup=true)).

[when:counts.unchecked_files] unchecked_files lists in-scope files no full-fidelity check covered (names_only / none extraction, or untracked). Verify those by reading them; never treat their absence of findings as clean.

[when:blocking] Blocking findings, fix order: (1) reconcile_paths(paths=<report.reconcile_paths>) catalogs untracked files and missing functions/types; (2) apply_audit_fixes(reason=..., report=<report_path>, apply=['repoint_interactions','missing_interactions','stale_interactions','stale_functions','stale_types','param_mismatch','malformed_json']) — mark deliberate indirect edges first (mark_indirect_ids); (3) update_function / update_type for incomplete prose; finalize_file(s) for reserved_files. Re-run audit_tracking to confirm.

[when:warnings] Warnings never block a task: unconfirmed_interactions and stale_descriptions need judgement; missing_type_links carry a suggested role (apply_audit_fixes apply=['missing_type_links'] after checking); structure_gaps are listed by get_structure_health.

[when:counts.exempted] exempted lists findings a person reviewed as not drift (audit_exemptions), with the reason and exemption_id; they never block. A finding carrying exemption_lapsed had an exemption whose function changed since: review it again, then re-exempt (unexempt_ids + exempt) or fix it.
[when:scope.schema_1_16=false] This database predates schema 1.16: run migrate_databases to enable audit exemptions (apply_audit_fixes exempt=[...]).

[when:counts.unbaselined_needs_review] Descriptions without a code hash were triaged: apply 'unbaselined_descriptions' for the ones that passed; review unbaselined_needs_review (reasons + code excerpt in the report) and fix or baseline_hash_function_ids them.
